name: Glendo State Park (Cottonwood Campground)
note: Cottonwood is a small campground in a cottonwood grove on the northeast shore of Glendo Reservoir, reached by a half-mile gravel road that turns north just before the Sandy Beach fee booth. Four of the five pads are natural sand ground under the trees, on a short spur off the gravel road, and may be soft going for a heavy rig; the paved pull-through (CW04) is the sure one. The lake rises into the grove at high water in late spring and early summer, then drops away. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: reserve.wyoming.gov (US eDirect API wyordr.usedirect.com/wyomingrdr/rdr/, PlaceId 10 'Glendo State Park', FacilityId 335 'Cottonwood', facility point 42.52898,-104.94163, read 2026-11-20): 10 web-bookable units - 5 'Campsite Non-Electric' CW02-CW06 (IsRVSite true; 'Unit & Parking Size(ft)' 45 on CW02/03/05/06, 140 on the paved ADA pull-through CW04; Rate 10.00; MaximumStay 14) + 5 Group Sites CW01, CW07, CW09 ('Sites included: 9 & 10'), CW11 ('11, 12, 13 combined'), CW14 -> real drive-in RV campground a 23-ft rig fits. Wyoming State Parks' own Cottonwood page (wyoparks.wyo.gov/index.php/about-our-campgrounds/1689-cottonwood-glendo, read as search-result text 2026-11-20; the site refuses with an F5 challenge): 14 sites in three areas, reached 'by turning north, just before the Sandy Beach Fee Booth and following the gravel road for a half mile'; no 4WD wording (unlike Broken Arrow's page or the Sandy Beach Dune sand units). Not in the DB: no name match; nearest entry 13976 Sandy Beach (FacilityIds 343/344, Willow centroid ~0.6 km S, Dune ~1.1 km S), a separate facility. Public (state): no price gate.
waterfront_evidence: 2026-11-20: Esri World Imagery frames at 300 m, 160 m, 100 m, 70 m and 110 m half-widths (0.25-0.6 m/px) with every reserve.wyoming.gov unit point (grid MapInfo, FacilityId 335) plotted; all images rendered. Imagery (leaf-off, drawn-down) shows CW02-CW06 on a sand spur at the inland (south) edge of a continuous cottonwood belt 60-100 m deep, the imaged water ~95-130 m north beyond the trees and a sand flat; CW07/CW09/CW11 (group units) on grass at the same belt's south edge; CW14 in a clearing over a rise to the east. Glendo full pool 4635.0 ft = 1413.51 m NAVD88 (glendo_notes.txt / lead 15). USGS 3DEP lidar (epqs.nationalmap.gov): unit points CW02 1417.6, CW03 1417.7, CW04 1418.5, CW05 1417.4, CW06 1417.1 m (3.6-5.0 m above full pool); the lidar's hydro-flattened water surface is 1412.98 m (flown ~0.5 m below full pool), and it reaches into the tree belt. Profiles to the full-pool contour: CW06 ~28 m N (1414.2 at 25 m, 1413.7 at 28 m), CW05 ~30-35 m N/NW, CW03 ~40 m, CW02 ~45-50 m N/NW; group units CW07/CW09 ~15-25 m, CW11 ~25 m, CW14 ~30 m N. So at high water the lake stands within ~30-50 m of the individual sites, but the whole span is inside the cottonwood stand (trees standing in the water at high pool), not an open apron; the park's page says the sites are 'a short walk from the water's edge' mid-May to mid/late July and that the cove 'is drained or in the process of draining' the rest of the year. A continuous treeline between pad and water is a buffer -> not lakefront; leaf-off imagery shows an open stand with a sand floor and no understory, the lake 30-50 m off and the pads 3.6-4 m above it on a gentle slope, so a filtered view through the trunks holds -> lakeview. The engine tags every unit 'Waterfront Setting: Reservoir' (type-level, as at Custer Cove).

flags: Sand: the park's own page says Cottonwood is 'Largely situated on the sand'; four of the five campsites list 'Parking Pad Material: None' (natural ground) and CW04 is paved. Imagery shows the pads on a short sand spur in the cottonwood grove, ~30 m off the maintained gravel park road - not an open beach, and no agency 4WD or sand-vehicle wording for Cottonwood (Sandy Beach Dune's sand units carry '4-wheel drives only or lighter vehicles are highly recommended'; Cottonwood's unit descriptions are blank). Kept under user_ekko_no_sand (maintained surface, not open beach) with the caveat in the note; if AWH reads the sand spur as too soft, CW04 (paved ADA pull-through) is the one sure pad.

Waterfront close call: lakeview, not lakefront. At full pool the water stands ~28 m from CW06, ~30-35 m from CW05 and ~40-50 m from CW02/CW03 (3DEP lidar), within the ~50 m bound, but the whole span is inside a continuous cottonwood stand that stands in the water at high pool - treated as a tree buffer. The reviewer may judge the leaf-off open stand as 'scattered trees' and raise CW05/CW06 to lakefront with a caveat naming them.
elevation_meters is Open-Meteo's 1410 m (the instruction source), which reads below Glendo full pool (1413.5 m); 3DEP lidar puts the pads at 1417.1-1418.5 m. Consider 1418.
